chapter.title: The present tense of -ir and -re verbs

grammar_rules.title: Regular -ir verbs (finir type) in the present tense
grammar_rules.summary: Drop -ir and add -is, -is, -it, -issons, -issez, -issent (with -iss- infix in plural).
grammar_rules.explanation: Regular 2nd group verbs (finir, choisir, remplir, réussir, obéir) take endings -is, -is, -it in singular, and insert -iss- before plural endings: -issons, -issez, -issent.
exceptions: Irregular short -ir verbs (partir, sortir) do not take -iss-

grammar_rules.title: Irregular short -ir verbs (partir, sortir, dormir type)
grammar_rules.summary: Singular stem drops the final consonant: je pars, tu pars, il part; plural stem keeps it: nous partons, vous partez, ils partent.
grammar_rules.explanation: Verbs like partir (je pars, nous partons), sortir (je sors, nous sortons), dormir (je dors, nous dormons), servir (je sers, nous servons), sentir (je sens, nous sentons), mentir (je mens, nous mentons) drop the final consonant of the root in the singular and restore it in the plural.

grammar_rules.title: Regular -re verbs (vendre type) in the present tense
grammar_rules.explanation: Regular -re verbs (vendre, attendre, descendre, entendre, perdre, rendre, répondre) add -s, -s, nothing in the 3rd person singular (il vend), and -ons, -ez, -ent in plural.
exceptions: prendre group, mettre, battre, etc. have different patterns
notes: Note that il/elle/on has NO ending added; it simply ends in the stem 'd' (il vend, elle attend).

common_mistakes.explanation: No 't' is added to 3rd person singular when stem ends in d.

grammar_rules.title: Conjugation of prendre and its compounds in the present tense
grammar_rules.summary: Prendre drops 'd' in nous/vous (prenons, prenez) and doubles 'n' in ils (prennent).
grammar_rules.explanation: Verbs of the prendre family (prendre, apprendre, comprendre, surprendre, entreprendre) conjugate: je prends, tu prends, il prend, nous prenons, vous prenez, ils prennent.

patterns: prends, prends, prend, prenons, prenez, prennent

grammar_rules.title: Three ways to ask a question in French
grammar_rules.summary: Questions can be formed by intonation (informal), 'est-ce que' (standard), or subject-verb inversion (formal).
grammar_rules.explanation:
1. Intonation: Tu parles français? (voice rises at end)
2. Est-ce que: Est-ce que tu parles français?
3. Inversion: Parles-tu français?
usage_conditions: Spoken informal, standard, and formal writing
notes: Add '-t-' in inversion when 3rd person singular verb ends in a vowel before il/elle/on: Parle-t-il? Aime-t-elle?

common_mistakes.explanation: Insert euphonic -t- between two vowel sounds in inversion.

grammar_rules.title: Basic negation with ne ... pas
grammar_rules.summary: Place 'ne' before the conjugated verb and 'pas' after it (n' before vowels).
grammar_rules.explanation: To make a sentence negative, place 'ne' (or 'n'') before the conjugated verb and 'pas' directly after: 'Il ne parle pas anglais'. In compound tenses, 'pas' precedes the past participle: 'Il n'a pas parlé'.

steps: Place ne / n' before conjugated verb

notes: Indefinite and partitive articles (un, une, des, du, de la) change to 'de / d'' in a direct negative, except with être.

common_mistakes.wrong: Je ne veux pas du vin
common_mistakes.correct: Je ne veux pas de vin

grammar_rules.title: Negative adverbs: ne... jamais, ne... plus, ne... rien, ne... personne
grammar_rules.explanation:
- ne... jamais: never
- ne... plus: no longer, not anymore
- ne... rien: nothing
- ne... personne: nobody / no one
Note: 'personne' follows the past participle in compound tenses (Je n'ai vu personne), whereas 'rien', 'plus', 'jamais' precede it (Je n'ai rien vu).

steps: Place negative word in place of pas

notes: Never combine 'pas' with 'jamais', 'plus', or 'rien' in standard French.

irregularity_notes: drops 'd' in plural, doubles 'n' in 3rd pl.

examples.french: Nous finissons notre travail à dix-huit heures.
examples.english: We finish our work at six o'clock.

examples.french: Ils partent en vacances demain matin.
examples.english: They are leaving on vacation tomorrow morning.

examples.french: Elle vend des fleurs sur le marché.
examples.english: She sells flowers at the market.

examples.french: Elle prend le métro tous les jours.
examples.english: She takes the subway every day.
